description: Interactive graph construction tool for Grade 7 Mathematics — Sports Survey Double Bar Graph. Redesigned with Singularity Design System. Blank graph canvas with 5 sport names on X-axis (Cricket, Basketball, Swimming, Hockey, Athletics). Y-axis with gridlines. Scale selector with 3 options (1 unit = 100, 200, or 250). For each sport, two bars: indigo (#4A4DC9) for Watching and orange (#FF7212) for Participating. Student types values to set heights. Correct bars lock with checkmark. Incorrect bars highlight and show expected value. After all 10 bars placed, an insights panel slides in showing: biggest watching sport (Cricket 1240), biggest gap (Cricket 620), smallest gap (Athletics 145), and overall pattern (watching > participating for all sports). Singularity design tokens: primary #4A4DC9, accent #FF7212, gradient #533086→#FC9145, tints #C1C1EA and #FFF3E4. Poppins font. Contained/Outlined/Highlight button variants with pill radius. Geometric shape decorations (circle, triangle, square, ellipse). Indian sports context. Mobile-responsive with horizontal scroll.

features.scaleSelection: 3 card options (1:100, 1:200, 1:250) with ★ BEST FIT badge using gradient pill. Singularity shadow.lg on hover. Geometric SVG decorations (circle + triangle + square from design system).
features.barConstruction: Sequential bar placement with value input, verification, and easeOutCubic animated growth. Active sport column highlighted with tintPurple dashed border and singGlow animation.
features.correctFeedback: Green (#22C55E) circle with animated checkmark stroke-draw. Contained-style success feedback card with #F0FDF4 background.
features.incorrectFeedback: singShake animation on input, red (#EF4444) circle with X icon, then auto-corrects showing correct value. Error card uses #FEF2F2 background.
features.insightsPanel: 4 animated insight cards with Lucide icons (Eye, BarChart3, Users, Sparkles). Each card has icon circle with 15% color fill, uses singSlidePanel stagger animation. Hover transforms translateX(4px) with tint background swap.
features.headerGradient: Animated gradient using #533086→#4A4DC9→#FC9145 with singGradientShift keyframe (8s cycle). Decorative geometric SVG shapes (circle, square, triangle, ellipse) at 8% opacity from design system.
features.buttonSystem: Three button variants matching Singularity PDF: Contained (#4A4DC9 fill, white text, pill radius), Outlined (primary border, transparent fill), Highlight (#FF7212 fill). All support Enabled/Disabled/Hover/Pressed states with scale transforms.
features.phaseIndicator: Dot + line progress indicator in header. Active dot stretches to 28px width. Completed segments use 50% white opacity. Smooth 0.4s cubic-bezier transitions.
features.dataTable: Reference data table with Singularity styling. Active sport column uses tintPurple 30% background. Active bar type row uses watching/participating color at 12% opacity.
features.progressBar: 8px rounded bar with primary→accent gradient fill. Smooth 0.5s width transition. Completion count in primary color bold text.
features.confetti: 24 particles using Singularity palette (primary, accent, tintPurple, success, deepPurple, gold). Mix of circles and rounded squares. singConfetti animation with rotation and scale-down.
features.responsiveDesign: Horizontal scroll for graph on mobile devices. Flexible padding with DS.spacing tokens.

keyframes.singGlow: box-shadow fade cycle with primary color

teachingNotes.scaleGuidance: Guide the student in scale selection: max value is 1240, so a scale of 200 works well (giving 7 rows on the y-axis). The ★ BEST FIT badge highlights this option.
teachingNotes.afterGraphDiscussion: After the graph is built, discuss: Cricket dominates in both watching (1240) and participating (620). The watching-participating gap is largest for Cricket (620 difference) and smallest for Athletics (145 difference).
discussionPrompts: Why do you think more people watch cricket than play it?
What about swimming — the gap is 190, quite modest!
Which sport has the biggest difference between watching and participating?
Can you think of reasons why athletics has such a small gap?
teachingNotes.indianSportsContext: Connect to Indian sports culture — cricket's dominance, hockey as national sport, growing athletics culture.

instructionsForStudent: The data shows how many people watch and participate in 5 sports. Your job: build a double bar graph! First, choose a scale that works for values up to 1240. Then set bar heights for Watching (indigo) and Participating (orange) for each sport. After building the graph, look at the gap between watching and participating — which sport has the biggest gap? The smallest?
